transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-06 15:00 UTC — Duration 54m. Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Daniel Ortega (CTO, Mariner), Maya Lee (Head of ML), Samir Patel (Infra), Rosa Chen (PM)

Summary: quick intro -> current infra & requirements -> models and context length discussion -> tool-calling + integrations -> security/compliance -> next steps. Deck link: https://redwood.app/decks/mariner-2027 (shared) 

[00:00] Jared: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros, we are Redwood, I do AE stuff, priya will cover infra and perf. can we go around real quick?
[00:12] Daniel: yeah, Daniel here, CTO at Mariner Health. we build patient triage and clinician-assist workflows. heavy PHI concerns, happy to be here.
[00:20] Maya: Maya, head of ML, i own model selection and eval — interested in multilingual support (EN/ES/FR) and long context for patient histories.
[00:28] Samir: Samir infra, we run on AWS but have strict VPC peering and private subnets, want to understand Redwood Private vs Dedicated.
[00:35] Priya: awesome thanks, outline: we'll ask about workloads, then walk models (open ones), context length needs, tool-calling (APIs/db access), and security.

[02:00] Priya: can you give us typical prompt patterns+context sizes? maybe avg tokens per request and tail cases?
[02:08] Maya: average ~600–800 tokens, but long clinics notes can be 6k–12k tokens, occasionally 25k. our hope is to support up to 64k ideally but at minimum 32k in the near term. some requests are streaming with tool calls to EHR.

[04:15] Jared: got it — so mix of short latency-y requests and long retrieval-heavy contexts. that informs model choice and routing; short ones might be served by smaller quantized models for cost, long ones need models with large context window or windowing + retrieval.

[06:30] Priya: on models — what are you evaluating now? open source choices?
[06:36] Maya: we've been testing Llama 3 70b, Mistral Mixtral 8x7b-ish, and Falcon 40b for hallucination behavior. cohort did some tests with a fine-tuned instruction-tuned variant. cost is a concern.
[06:55] Jared: common tradeoffs — Llama 3 variants give strong instruction tuning but bigger mem/latency; Mistral models are efficient but sometimes struggle on long-range coherence; Falcon sits in between. Redwood supports all these and can route to quantized variants.

[08:12] Samir: question on KV cache and long contexts — we need to know whether the runtime keeps KV in memory between calls or streams to ssd for huge contexts. what is your recommendation?
[08:25] Priya: Redwood runtime uses GPU KV cache for active generation and supports prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, plus optional disk-backed checkpoints for very large pass-throughs — there is some overhead. for 64k you typically need model variants compiled with long-context kernels or segmented generation + retrieval. we call it continuous batching + smart caching.

[10:40] Maya: are there quantized 8-bit or 4-bit options for Llama-3 or Falcon that you recommend? we need to balance quality for clinical summ and cost.
[10:50] Priya: yes we have quantization profiles, Redwood Optimize can recommend 4-bit quantized for high-throughput low-latency calls, but for sensitivity tasks we suggest FP16 or 4-bit with per-channel calibration. we can run a quick eval on your test set to show quality delta.

[13:00] Rosa: tool-calling — we need to have model call external tools: EHR read-only, a meds-check microservice, and a simple patient-data redact utility. how is that done?
[13:15] Jared: Redwood supports structured tool calling via JSON schemas, function calling style, and a controlled plugin interface. you can set policies so tool calls only happen after guardrail checks.
[13:30] Maya: any latency numbers for tool-calling round trips? in some flows we need sub-300ms total.
[13:40] Priya: depends — hosted can give sub-200ms generation for short prompts on lightweight models; tool roundtrip adds network latency — for internal calls inside a VPC with Dedicated you can get more predictable sub-200–300ms. Private on-prem will depend on your infra and connection to the runtime.

[16:10] Daniel: security is big — SOC2, ISO, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and HSM for keys. we need docs and a 3rd party pen test history.
[16:25] Jared: we will send SOC2 and ISO reports, audit log samples, and KMS integration guide. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS / HSM. Dedicated supports dedicated GPU pools with encryption and audit retention choices.

[18:05] Samir: network details: our infra requires no outbound internet from the inference environment and strict egress controls. can Redwood Private be fully air-gapped?
[18:15] Priya: Private can be deployed in your VPC with zero outbound allowed to the public internet; air-gapped on-prem options exist as well but require longer lead time. we do have an on-prem package for regulated workloads.

[20:00] Maya: model versioning and rollouts — we need canary testing and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes.
[20:10] Priya: Redwood Console supports per-route rollouts (canary/A-B), automatic fallback policies to compatible variants, and token-level cost/latency dashboards so you can set thresholds for rollback.

[22:35] Daniel: how do you handle multilingual? we need parity across EN/ES/FR and some PT-BR.
[22:45] Priya: we recommend evaluating multilingual instruction-tuned variants and run evals on your language-specific eval sets. We often route EN traffic to tuned EN models and use multilingual models for other languages, but for parity you may want a single capable model, which increases cost. Redwood Optimize can recommend per-language routing to balance quality/cost.

[25:00] Jared: benchmarking — we'd like to run a perf benchmark with 3 model candidates on your 8k sample set: Llama-3 70B-ft, Mistral-X (mixed-context), and Falcon-40B-ql. Would you be okay sharing a sanitized sample?
[25:12] Maya: yes we can produce a deidentified set of 200 patient interactions; Samir will coordinate transfer.

[27:20] Samir: cost question — hosted is easiest but we are worried about PHI. Dedicated seems attractive for mixed workloads, private for full compliance. ballpark delta?
[27:35] Jared: hosted is lowest up-front, per-token; Dedicated has predictable monthly commit and lower per-token at scale; Private has platform fee + infra costs. we'll send a TCO worksheet comparing 6/12/24 month scenarios and a sample SKU for Dedicated GPU pools.

[30:10] Rosa: integration points — we need an SDK for backend services, webhooks for async jobs, and RBAC for routes.
[30:20] Priya: we have SDKs (Python/Node), webhook support, and route-level RBAC with SSO. we'll include sample snippets in the follow-up.

[33:00] Maya: any pitfalls you see with our plan to have a mix of short queries and very long summary jobs?
[33:10] Priya: main pitfalls are cost if you serve all at high context, and latency unpredictability for large contexts. two patterns work well: 1) retrieval-augmented generation with semantic retrieval to keep active context small, and 2) specialized long-context model pipelines for batch summarization. Redwood supports both and can stitch them with smart routing.

[36:45] Daniel: compliance checklist — we also want to know about data retention, purge controls, and access logging.
[36:55] Jared: retention is configurable per workspace, you can set auto-purge, and all actions are logged with exportable audit trails. we'll share the retention and purge docs.

[40:00] Maya: can you run a small POC with Dedicated reserved capacity for 1 month? we want to test tool-calling and KV cache behavior under real load.
[40:10] Jared: yes we can propose a POC: 4 GPU Dedicated pool, pre-configured VPC peering, 200k tokens/day for 30 days, benchmarks + quality evals. I'll sketch pricing and a SOW.

[43:20] Priya: technical deep-dive follow-up — recommend scheduling 2h next Wed with your infra and security folks to go through VPC peering, subnets, firewall, and KMS setup.

[44:35] Samir: ok Samir will do network constraints doc and Maya will send eval set.

[46:00] Jared: recap — we'll send: pricing POV (hosted/dedicated/private TCO), SOC2/ISO docs + KMS integration guide, Redwood Optimize sample suggestions, and a proposed POC SOW. Priya will produce an example rollout config and perf checklist.

[47:30] Rosa: timeline — target POC start in 2 weeks, decision maker loop is 4–6 weeks.

[49:00] Maya: quick q — do you have examples of customers with similar PHI flows?
[49:10] Liam: yes, anonymized case studies we can share; I'll include 2 references and a redacted benchmark sheet.

[51:00] Daniel: great — thanks, that was helpful.
[51:10] Jared: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with docs and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
